text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are computer programs that understand and produce human language. They work by predicting the next word in a sentence, based on patterns learned from huge amounts of training data, such as books, websites and articles. Users can guide an LLM by writing clear instructions, which is called prompt engineering. LLMs can answer questions, summarize texts and help with writing. However, they also have limits: they may give wrong information, cannot check facts on their own, and their knowledge stops at a certain date.
